steps.text: Preheat an oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease a baking sheet liberally with olive oil.

Place the salmon fillets onto the baking sheet skin-side-down. Sprinkle the fillets with garlic powder, dill, salt, and pepper. Lay the bacon strips over the fillets to cover completely. Do not overlap the bacon strips.
Bake in the preheated oven until the salmon is no longer translucent in the center, 20 to 25 minutes. Turn the oven on to broil and cook until the bacon has crisped, 1 to 2 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Bacon-Wrapped Salmon
raw_recipe.description: What more is there to say? The salmon stays really moist from the bacon, and the skin helps protect the bottom from cooking prematurely.
raw_recipe.name: Bacon-Wrapped Salmon

Bake in the preheated oven until the salmon is no longer translucent in the center, 20 to 25 minutes. Turn the oven on to broil and cook until the bacon has crisped, 1 to 2 minutes.

review.reviewBody: The way I see it, adding bacon to ANYTHING is a good thing and adding it to salmon is a great thing! This is a wonderful quick and tasty dish. I sliced some potatoes and added them to the pan. In a separate skillet I sauted up some zuchinni, summer squash, tomato, onion, and garlic which made a nice side dish to compliment the fish. Everyone should try this recipe. You won't be disappointed!

Omg! Yes yes and YES!!!
Only 2 changes made. First one was cutting the filets into skinnier pieces, I rolled up the fish then wrapped 1 whole slice of bacon around it, securing the end with a toothpick. I tried the flat way and it used up 2 pieces of bacon to wrap it. The 3nd change is instead of any seasonings in the recipe, I brushed them with Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ sauce that I added 3 Tablespoons of good bourbon to. The only response I got when my dinner mates ate these is "Wow"!!!

Changed it a bit. Used two wild salmon filets 1/2 lb. each. Seasoned the filets with lemon zest, sprigs of fresh tarragon, sea salt and fresh ground pepper. Cooked the thick cut bacon some before cooling and wrapping salmon horizontally around the filets. Put filets in an oven proof pan with melted cooking fat on stove for 2 mins. ea. side on high heat to brown bacon. Put pan in oven at 375 for about 8-10 mins. Garnished with lemon and served on bed of mixed greens and served with thin green beans. Best ever.

Superb! I followed the recipe to a tee, adding brussel sprouts and new potatoes on each side of the baking sheet. I had some thick salmon fillets, so I added another 10 minutes to the baking time and broiled for five minutes while rotating the pan. It looked and tasted like a gourmet meal from a fancy restaurant! Could not have been happier. This recipe is definitely a keeper!

I was skeptical, since it was unrated, but it certainly sounded good! I had a fine filet, almost one pound, and cut it into two. I added the garlic powder, dill, salt and pepper, then covered each one with half-slices of thick-sliced bacon so that it looked like the picture above. Baked at 375 for about 20 - 22 min., then broiled carefully on high, at about 6-inches below the broiler until the bacon was crisp--about 4 - 5 minutes. (Don't ignore it, or let it get away!) The result? Splendid! Best salmon filets I have ever had! These were nice big 8 oz filets with good thick bacon, and were a real treat, worthy of professional offering as a seafood main course !

This is a often asked for dinner in our house. I usually baste the salmon with brown sugar and maple syrup before putting the bacon on and then again on top of the bacon. Serve it with wild rice that has a few squirts of siracha and everyone is happy.

I normally grill my fish on the BBQ, but today I wanted to try something different and stumbled across this recipe. It's delicious! But that's a given, considering it's topped with bacon! I personally think 20-25 mins is a little long. Instead, I increased the temp to 425 for the first 5 mins, then 400 for another 10 mins and the salmon was perfectly cooked and moist, plus the bacon was just how I like it. No need to broil at the end. I wasn't that hungry, but I ended up eating both pieces I made because it was so good! I didn't even have a chance to take a pic. Next time!

Did this tonight, and found it magnificent!! It was excellent with fresh dill rather than dried, just for you to know, and it was great. Not all recipes are great, often they're missing ingredients, or the time for the cooking is off, or worse, things you'd never put in a dish together!! This however was true to form, good food!! Also, wanted to let you know, that my salmon was frozen solid, and this did not affect anything, other than you'll need to increase the time in the oven by 5-10 minutes. It needs to be cooked through with a little firm to touch so you know it's done. WARNING: make more than you think you'll need, because family will want seconds on this one!!

This was delicious. 

Because I'm lazy I put asparagus drizzled with a little oil and salt under the salmon so it cook at the same time and cooked for 25 min, then broiled as others did. Served with a side of cauliflower mash. Thanks for the recipe.
I left the bacon strips whole and wrapped it the whole way around the fillet and cooked it like it says it was delicious with a little homemade tarter sauce on top!! Very good!! ;)

This is a wonderful recipe. I followed all the recipe directs and ingredients. I did use a oven rake to cook my salmon on as suggested by another reviewer. Why? because I love the crispy crunch of salmon skin. This recipe makes the best baked salmon I have ever eaten. It was flaky and juicy and just Delicious. Salmon filet is often dry when fully cooked. Next time I cook this I'm going to try a maple bacon. A big point in trying this recipe is its simple with seasonings that you normally have on hand or are easy to acquire. I don't think it matters what you serve with it because this salmon is the star of the show.
Yummy!! Very easy, will definitely make again
Easy and delicious! Added to my favorite salmon recipes.
I added my little twist but it came out delicious! For bacon lovers, you got to try this!

I've been using this recipe for 9 years now, (for as long as I've been married) it's the only recipe I continually follow. My husband requests it for every special occasion. The only thing I ever do different is double the spice mixture because we love it so much. 

I usually roast veggies as a side along with it.
Delicious! Broiling truly made the bacon crispy and the bacon dripped into the salmon

Giving this 3 stars is generous. I have Salmon twice a week, love this fish, I have a lot of very good recipes but enjoy checking new ones out. What a way to ruin a beautiful piece of fillet, the seasoning is lost and all you have is a bacon grease covered fish, mind you anything tastes better with bacon and that’s what you really taste ...is bacon with a hint of greasy salmon. People move on from this recipe!
This was so amazing! The dill and the bacon worked really well with the salmon. Made it exactly as written. This is a keeper.
